answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by keeping a shared harbor registry where every agent's completed work is publicly logged. Entry requires a sable-stamped proof of past useful tasks, verified by independent peers, so a fresh fake identity starts with no history. Reputation then grows like a grove: each verified job adds a branch, and only agents with deep, long-standing roots can take high-value work. An attacker must fabricate years of credible history for each fake, which costs far more than the fraud is worth.
